title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants
abstract: arXiv:2611.28914v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Sanctions screening raises name-based alerts that are mostly false positives, and level-1 analysts clear them by checking the customer's date of birth and name against a written policy. We test whether open-weight language models that a bank can run on its own premises can perform this level-1 disposition. From the UK and EU sanctions lists (7,103 natural persons) we built 12,200 synthetic customers: listed persons under six name conditions, including Turkish spellings of Arabic-origin names and Turkish romanisations of Cyrillic names, and two date-of-birth conditions, plus namesakes, near-name customers and a general population. A deterministic fuzzy and embedding screen raised 7,383 alerts, which three open models served on domestic infrastructure and three rule baselines dispositioned under the same policy. The models sent far fewer innocent customers to level 2 than a rule that applies the policy's date clause: 0.6 to 16.9 per 1,00

translated_title: 开源大语言模型能否清除制裁筛查警报？基于公开制裁名单与土耳其姓名变体的预注册测试
translated_abstract: 制裁筛查会产生大量基于姓名的警报，其中大多是误报，一级分析师需依据书面政策核对客户出生日期和姓名来清除这些警报。我们测试了银行可在本地部署的开源权重语言模型能否执行这一一级处置任务。我们从英国和欧盟制裁名单（7,103名自然人）中构建了12,200个合成客户：涵盖六种姓名条件下列入名单的人员（包括阿拉伯语姓名的土耳其语拼写以及西里尔字母姓名的土耳其语罗马化形式）和两种出生日期条件，并加入同名者、近似姓名客户及普通人群。一个确定性的模糊匹配与嵌入筛查产生了7,383条警报，三个开源模型在本地基础设施上提供服务，与三个规则基线在相同政策下进行处置。相比执行政策日期条款的规则，模型将无辜客户送往二级审查的数量要少得多：每1,000条中仅为0.6至16.9条。
tldr: 该预注册测试表明，可在本地部署的开源大语言模型能够执行制裁筛查警报的一级处置任务，即使面对土耳其语姓名变体等复杂情况，误送无辜客户至二级审查的比例也远低于基于规则的基线方法。
en_tdlr: This pre-registered test demonstrates that open-weight LLMs deployable on-premises can perform level-1 sanctions screening alert disposition, sending far fewer innocent customers to level-2 review than rule-based baselines, even with challenging Turkish name variants.
